lines.0: Hello Nisha, I’m Asha, your AI teacher. Today we’ll learn fractions as equal shares. What music do you enjoy?
lines.1: You enjoy dancing to Bollywood songs with Riya, especially “Kala Chashma”—that sounds lively. Imagine sharing one roti equally: what might happen?
lines.2: Keep explaining your idea, Nisha.
lines.3: A third means three equal parts; if one is smaller, it is not one-third. How can you make all three equal?
lines.4: Go on, Nisha—notice what must match.
lines.5: Keep going with the three equal pieces, Nisha.
lines.6: Try finding three equal parts, Nisha.
lines.7: Look at the circle: imagine three same-sized slices meeting at its centre. Point to one slice.
lines.8: Yes, Nisha, one colour is one equal part. How many pencils belong in each third of 15?
lines.9: Let’s separate two ideas: the number of groups and the pencils in one group. What is 1/3 of 15 pencils? Fill the gap: 1/3 means 1 of ___ equal groups.
lines.10: You got “1 of 3 equal groups” right. A rope is cut into 3 pieces of different lengths. Is each piece one-third of the rope?
lines.11: Right—the three pieces must be equal. Why must the pieces be equal: to make equal shares, or just to have three pieces?
lines.12: Exactly, Nisha: equal shares need pieces of the same size. Two same-sized rectangular school flags each have 4 coloured sections. Flag A has 4 equal sections; F
lines.13: You counted the other sections, but a fraction counts the chosen part out of all equal parts. On which flag is one section definitely one-quarter: A or B?
lines.14: This question is tricky; that is okay. Look for the flag whose four parts are equal. On which flag is one section definitely one-quarter: A or B?
